items.t: **Claude Code shipped a native session dashboard** (Agent View, May 2026): every session listed with alive / dormant / sleeping status, warm restart from disk, plus a JSON command for scripting external status bars.
**Statuslines are the dominant lightweight pattern:** token percent, cost, branch and reset countdown in the prompt, color-thresholded (green under 50, yellow 50, orange 70, red 90).
**ccusage** is the de facto usage tool: parses local session logs, zero API calls, daily / weekly / five-hour-block reports.
**Kanban-over-Claude-Code and "mission control" fleets** exist; both serve multi-agent swarms. **Approval-queue inboxes** with single-key approve / reject are the human-in-the-loop standard.
**1 · A budget bar** in the header, color-thresholded. Small.
**2 · A git-diff changelog** in Block 0, generated by the build, not narrated. Small.
**3 · Cache the static panels** (Deep Stacks, the SOI card) so they are never rewritten. Small.
**4 · Single-key approve / defer / reject** on Block V. Small.
**5 · Agent View's status words** on the Ancients instead of bare dates. Small.
**6 · Build-side diff of the board JSON** so only changed panels get new explainer text. Medium; the biggest token saver.
**7 · Local token parsing** the ccusage way, plus a five-hour reset countdown. Medium.
**8 · A terminal statusline** with the same bar. Small, separate from the page.
Multi-agent fleets · live localhost servers · enterprise approval machinery with audit trails and risk tiers. Take the single-key UX, leave the governance.
